message:
docs: design of agent definitions (agents you define)

A defined agent is an engine (claude or codex), a model and standing
instructions in a Markdown file, usable wherever an agent name is.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01RDemkNgnazAvXXCCuUFomL

docs: an agent definition's engine is optional

Without an engine the agent runs on the user's default engine, so one
definition works for a whole team; a model needs a pinned engine.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01RDemkNgnazAvXXCCuUFomL

feat: agent definitions - agents made of an engine, a model and instructions

A Markdown file in the config folder's agents/ or a trusted project's
.flint/agents defines an agent usable wherever an agent name is: chats,
agent tasks, defaultAgent and start_agent. The engine is optional; without
it the agent runs on the default native agent. Instructions reach Claude
Code as --append-system-prompt and Codex as developerInstructions. A
session records its engine and resumes on it.

The frontend still calls AgentChatAPI.Resume without the engine; the next
commit updates it.

feat: defined agents in pickers, Settings and the command palette

Chats save their engine and pass it to Resume. Pickers label a defined
agent with its engine, Settings ▸ Agents lists the definitions with their
problems, and New Agent Definition… creates one and opens it. A prompt
limited to an agent also applies to defined agents on that engine.

fix: review findings on agent definitions

- Loading the definitions is serialized from reading the files to
  registering them, so an older read can't register what a newer one
  removed (a definition of a folder untrusted in between).
- A review agent that names a defined agent no longer available falls
  back to the default agent instead of failing every review.
- New Agent… may create a personal definition under a project one's name.
- The conflict tooltip no longer says a defined agent has no terminal
  mode when the terminal runs its engine.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01RDemkNgnazAvXXCCuUFomL

feat: reviews carry a defined agent's instructions; a chat starts on its own read

- Review Changes with Agent passes the instructions of a defined review
  agent (Claude: --append-system-prompt, Codex: -c developer_instructions
  as a TOML string). Commit messages and Edit with Agent still run
  without them: their answers have a fixed format.
- A chat starts or resumes on the definition its own call read. Defined
  agents are no longer registered with the session manager by name; the
  manager is handed the driver (StartWith, ResumeWith).
- An orchestration role for claude or codex fits a defined agent on that
  engine.
- One call reads the definitions once (agentView).

test: trust the resolved folder in the defined agents tests

On macOS a temp folder is reached through a symbolic link (/var →
/private/var), and trust compares resolved paths, so the project
definition was not loaded there and three tests failed.

feat: model tiers for defined agents (fast, balanced, strong)

A definition can name a tier instead of a model, with or without an
engine; agents.<engine>.tiers maps each tier to a model. Claude Code
defaults to haiku, sonnet and opus; Codex has no defaults, so an
unmapped tier keeps the engine's model. The tier resolves on the engine
the conversation runs on, on start, on resume and in headless runs.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01RDemkNgnazAvXXCCuUFomL

feat: backlog - work items above repositories, delegated to agents (Go side)

A backlog is a folder with flint-backlog.json and items/*.md. Delegate
starts one agent task per repository an item names, with the agent it
names; the item's status follows its agent tasks (doing, review, done)
and is written to its file. Repositories are matched to checkouts by
remote URL. A read-only agent tool, get_backlog, lists the items.

The feature contract is widened on purpose: a TasksChanged hook and Host
methods for agent tasks, repositories and agents.

fix: review findings on the backlog

- A repository resolves to a trusted checkout before an untrusted one that
  claims the same URL; the trust question says it trusts the whole folder.
- An item moves by itself only when its agent tasks changed, so a status
  the user set stays; links of an item whose file is missing are kept.
- Tasks of a Delegate in progress are held back from the queue, so a
  rollback can't remove a task whose chat already started.
- A backlog in an untrusted folder is left out of get_backlog, and
  Delegate from it asks first, showing what the agent will get.
- Items with invisible or control characters are problems; limits are in
  bytes everywhere; detached HEAD has a message Delegate can act on.
- The panel lists the repositories with Locate…, Add to Workspace and
  Trust Folder…; group headers work from the keyboard; the Delegate
  walk-through says what it asks for and why it stops.
- The guide and the design match the UI.
